name: JanusGraph
tagline: Open-source distributed graph database layered on Cassandra, HBase, ScyllaDB or Bigtable.
description: JanusGraph is a Linux Foundation project, forked from Titan in 2017, that turns a wide-column store (Cassandra, ScyllaDB, HBase, Bigtable) or BerkeleyDB into a TinkerPop-compatible graph database. Indexes for full-text, geo and range queries are delegated to Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Solr or Lucene, and Spark-based OLAP is available through TinkerPop's GraphComputer. It scales to very large graphs because storage scales horizontally, but operators must run and tune two or three distributed systems, and release cadence is slow (1.1.0 in late 2024, with 1.2.0 staged in October 2026).

pricing.notes: Free; cost comes from operating the storage and index backends.

scale.notes: Inherits scale and multi-DC replication from the storage backend (e.g. Cassandra or ScyllaDB).

strengths: Fully open source under Apache 2.0 with neutral foundation governance
Scales storage horizontally by delegating to Cassandra, ScyllaDB, HBase or Bigtable
Pluggable mixed indexes (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Solr) for full-text and geo predicates
Standard TinkerPop/Gremlin, so tooling and queries port to other Gremlin databases
weaknesses: Running JanusGraph means operating a storage cluster and an index cluster as well
Traversal latency is higher than native graph engines because each hop hits a KV backend
ACID guarantees depend on the backend and are weak on eventually consistent stores
Slow release cadence and a small core maintainer team
useCases: Large-scale graphs on existing Cassandra or ScyllaDB clusters
Open-source alternative to managed Gremlin services
notIdealFor: Small teams without distributed-systems ops experience
